rows.hook_shape: TWO instruments, both cheap, both fitting patterns already in CodePatches.cpp. (1) LOG - a naked log-and-relay hook at 0x6D4860, the SpAttachDetour/SpStripDetour idiom exactly (pushad/pushfd, push args, call a __stdcall logger, popfd/popad, jmp trampoline; never a typed prototype, per the project's thiscall law for unknown arity). At entry it can read everything needed without touching the mid-function frame: ecx = this, and the {3,7,0xB} selector is simply stack arg1 - disassembly today shows edi is loaded at 0x6D486B from [esp+0x20], which after sub esp,0xC + four pushes is entry esp+4. So log this, [esp+4], [esp+8] and the return address; behind pushad+pushfd those sit at [esp+40] / [esp+44]. (2) SUPPRESSION - a 4-byte immediate swap at 0x6D4A67 (the operand of the push at 0x6D4A66, stock bytes 00 00 F1 29), rewritten to a nonexistent instance such as 0x29F1FFFF so the exemplar fetch misses and no arrow is created. Verify-before-write against the stock dword, single VirtualProtect span, always log the resolved value - the ApplyCsiIndicatorScale house pattern. This is the safe suppression: an early return at 0x6D4860 is NOT safe, because the arity is unknown and a naked hook cannot pick the right ret N. Residual risk to state up front: a deliberately-missing exemplar takes a game code path nobody has exercised; if it faults, the finding is still the finding, but run it after the log-only pass, never before.
rows.proof_needed: A TIMING MATCH, not a count match - it is strictly stronger and immune to the 'was it already there at load?' ambiguity. With the log hook armed, drag one new road to a city edge that borders another region tile and accept the neighbour-connection prompt: the mechanism predicts EXACTLY ONE new line from 0x6D4860 at that instant, and none while nothing is being built. Read the count prediction in the same launch as the cheap corroborator (N arrows visible on screen = N lines since load) and the zero-connection city as the negative control. The suppression pass then converts it to an absence: swap the instance imm, relaunch the same city, and every edge arrow must be gone while the roads, the signposts and the zots all still draw. Two free riders in the same capture: (a) the logged selector value turns the unresolved edi in {3,7,0xB} into a measurement - build a road connection, then a rail one, and read which value each produces; (b) the TIER CALL is a prediction in its own right and needs no code at all - world-anchored predicts the arrow roughly doubles in screen pixels per zoom step, pixel-fixed predicts equal px, so two screenshots at adjacent zooms adjudicate 'n-a, do not patch' on the spot. This is unusually clean because the null is already banked and pinned: all twelve 2026-08-17 captures carry 'SPPROBE strip hook armed on 0x005F5FB0' as the positive control and SPSTRIP fire count = 0, because no route query was ever performed in any captured session. design.risks:
CRASH / SAVE RISKS, worst first.

1. DOTKILL early return at 0x5F7C80 — THE ONE ITEM THAT CAN CRASH FROM OUR OWN CODE. The shipped detour is NAKED and the function's arity is unknown, so an early return cannot pick the right `ret N`; a wrong guess corrupts the stack and the game dies. MITIGATION: do not build it until the epilogue's ret immediate has been read from the image. If it cannot be read unambiguously, DROP IT — DotSize=0.02 gives the identical on-screen absence with zero stack exposure, and the row's whole argument (four callers, no vtable refs, all in class B) applies just as well to the rebuild site. This is exactly the "drop it if the prize is small" case.

2. NBORARROW imm swap (NborArrow=2) — deliberately making an exemplar fetch MISS takes a game code path nobody has ever exercised, at city load, for every edge connection. It can fault, and it faults early. MITIGATION: it is not in rounds 1-3 at all. The row's PRIMARY proof is the timing match from the log-only hook, and the tier call needs no code whatsoever (two adjacent-zoom screenshots). My recommendation is to not run it: the marginal prize is converting a timing match into an absence, and the cost of being wrong is a dead session. If it is run, it gets its own short launch, alone, with no saving.

3. ZONEQUAD kill (ZoneQuadProbe=2) — skipping the lot-display quad builder leaves display objects that later code may expect to be populated. It runs at city load for every zoned lot, so a fault surfaces immediately rather than mid-session. MITIGATION: log-only in round 1 first (which also supplies the mandatory counter), kill in round 3, and DO NOT SAVE the city afterwards. Zone data itself is untouched — this only skips the display build — but an unsaved session costs nothing to discard.

4. LOG-VOLUME STALL, not a crash but it can ruin a round. 0x5E90E0 can be called per-occupant per-frame; an unconditional line per call would flood the log and stall the render thread badly enough to look like a hang. The design logs only on mode CHANGE plus a running total every 500 calls. Similarly ViewListRepeat must be 300, not 90 — the existing code clamps 1-29 to 30, which is far too fast once four layer lists are being written to disk every second.

5. VIEWKILL mid-walk removal — already correct in the shipped code (`next` is read at :8246 BEFORE the RemoveViewObject call at :8253). Do not reorder those two lines when touching anything nearby; reversing them would walk a freed node.

6. EFFECTFILTER restructure — the kill must return 0 and MUST NOT write *out. The exe writes *ppOut at exactly one site (0x593AB9, success) and never on a failure path, so a suppressed spawn is indistinguishable from a stock "no such effect"; writing a null there instead would be a behaviour the exe never produces. Note also the census log block must stay BEFORE the early return, or a killed name produces silence and the absence becomes unattributable.

7. TWO SEQUENCING TRAPS that silently destroy findings rather than crashing. (a) Row 13's `local_` effect kill and the 0x6CC970 kill must NEVER be armed in the same launch — arming both erases both halves and the SPLIT, which is the entire prediction, cannot be observed. (b) SC4UIScaleDllDirector.cpp:1220 gates the ViewListRepeat arm behind spikeScaleAll, so a 1x control launch arms nothing and produces a guaranteed silent null; the one-line fix is in the VIEWLIST probe notes and must ship in this build or row 8 can fail with no line saying why.

8. DEPLOY, not runtime: the game runs elevated and holds the DLL open, so the build must be copied on close, never by killing the process.
design.notes:
SHARED DRAWERS — where the work collapses. Nine rows do NOT need nine probes.

* FOUR ROWS, ONE DETOUR. Rows 11 (service-radius circles), 12 (lot direction arrow), 14 (terrain brush ring) and the DRAG half of row 13 (local_grid / local_tile_outline) all spawn through CreateEffectByName 0x5939B0, and that detour ALREADY SHIPS. The only new code is a name-prefix filter and an ini-tunable census cap — perhaps 40 lines. Each row's positive control is its own surviving siblings, so all three name families can be killed in the SAME launch (round 2) without contaminating each other. That is the single biggest saving in the plan.

* TWO ROWS, ONE MODULE. Rows 4 and 16 are the two view classes of the same signpost-occupant module, and the shipped SPPROBE arm (MissionBubbleFx=3) already installs both channels — SPATTACH on class B's 0x5F7C80 and SPSTRIP on class A's 0x5F5FB0. They must be in the same launch, because row 4's outcome IS row 16's answer: if the dots survive the class-B lever, they belong to class A's strip path, which MARKERZOOM already scales, and row 4 collapses into row 16.

* ONE ROW, ZERO CODE. Row 8 needs nothing built — VIEWOBJ, VIEWLIST and VIEWKILL all ship. Two ini keys and one gating fix.

* ONE ROW RIDES FOR FREE EVERYWHERE. Row 10 is reachable in the first ten seconds of any city with no mission, no cheat and nothing built, so its hook is armed in every round at no gesture cost.

Net new code: one filter engine inside an existing detour, three new hooks (0x5E90E0, 0x5F7810, 0x6D4860 + the 0x6CC970 kill), two small addenda to an existing logger, and one one-line gating fix.

WHY THE FIRST ROUND IS PURE CENSUS. Every one of these rows has a recorded false-null in its history — the SPATTACH capture with no mission active, the BUBBLEALL budget spent at city load, the ViewListRepeat key that armed nothing, the row-11 probe that would have read the wrong field. Suppression is the primary instrument, but a suppression whose positive control was never established is a bare absence. Round 1 buys every control in one sitting at zero risk; rounds 2 and 3 then spend them.

ROUND 2 AND 3 NEED NO REBUILD. Everything after round 1 is ini-only, so if a round goes sideways the recovery is editing a text file, not a build-deploy cycle. That was a deliberate design constraint: the one build carries every lever, and the launches choose between them.

THE ROW-11 TRAP, restated because it would have cost a session: do NOT implement that row file's own proposed probe (log [instance+0x110] one frame after the spawn, expect 2x radius). The doubled radius goes into the transform block at [esp+0x78] and is delivered via vt+0x20 at 0x4C2798; +0x110 keeps its constructor default of 1.0, and row 12 independently proves the same system never writes it. That probe would read 1.0 and be misread as the model being wrong — a false null manufactured by reading the wrong field.

TIER: run rounds 1-3 at 1.5x, not 1x. Row 16's table=1.125 prediction needs a scaling tier, and until the gating fix ships the ScaleAll conjunct at DllDirector.cpp:1220 would leave a 1x launch with nothing armed.
